speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: For the purpose of today's Adjournment Motion, I will be focusing my speech on "E", the "Embracing Parenthood" component, as the preservation and strengthening of family ties are an important part of our Singapore society.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: In support, the Alliance for Action to Strengthen Marriages and Family Relation (AFAM) introduced an initiative for Singaporeans to pledge and commit towards strengthening our family bonds.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: In this pledge, one agrees, among others, to make time for one another, show love, care and concern, and support one another through good times and bad.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: To help families and individuals turn these pledges into reality, I hope to take this opportunity to highlight some of the feedback which my Woodgrove residents and our PAP Women's Wing activists have shared with me pertaining to the challenges which many Singaporeans are facing as parents with young children, along with some recommendations on possible ways that the Government, employers and the community can play a supportive role in their own capacities, as well as suggestions to jumpstart new initiatives that aim to do so.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: For the past two years, during my engagements through regular house visits and thematic townhalls, I have had numerous opportunities to interact with many of my Woodgrove residents who are working parents.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Out of the 11 zones of Residents' Network in Woodgrove, we have three zones comprising HDB BTO flats which were completed within the last 10 years.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: They are Tree Trail and Tree Grove at our Woodgrove Zone 3, Champions Court at Zone 4 and Woodlands Peak at Zone 10.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Another two BTO projects are currently under construction, these being Champions Green and Woodgrove Ascent.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Most of the residents who are residing in these BTO flats have infant children.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Many of them are small families with both parents holding full-time jobs, including working mummies who are about to return to work after fully utilising their maternity leave and would usually seek my assistance in securing a placement for their child in infant care.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: While their own circumstances are unique, they all share the same dilemma, in that due to work commitment, they can no longer be always around to care for their little ones.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: They hope to entrust their child to a safe location, with responsible caregivers and, hopefully, within close proximity to their residences and at affordable rates.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Many of them have searched high and low for such a facility but to no avail and are desperate for a solution when they came looking for help.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Recently, a resident sought for my help to obtain a placement in an infant care centre for her seven-month-old daughter.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: The child's grandmother used to look after her on behalf of the family but changing circumstances have made this arrangement no longer possible.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Both the resident and her husband are also holding jobs that require on-site work, which meant that, without support, one of them would need to give up their job to look after their child.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: In another case, a resident shared with me that his family is facing difficulties in securing a slot in the preschool just below their residence for their two-year-old son.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: They had applied last year but were informed that the infant care centres are full and have a waitlist stretching to 2023.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: In addition, the pandemic has required them to care for their son and new-born daughter without support from other family members who reside overseas.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Although both he and his wife are employed, they had made it work thus far by hiring a helper and relying on his wife's maternity leave.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: But their time is running out as the helper is returning to her hometown and the agency is still sourcing for a new replacement for them, with the whole process likely to take many more months.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: I sympathise with my residents going through such challenging tough situations.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Currently, these spaces have looked into providing mental health screening and support for youth with mental health issues and operating a strength training gym for the seniors.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: It would be ideal if such community spaces can also be offered to preschools and non-profit organisations to provide after-school care services to support working parents, especially single parents and those who are on shift work.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: One exemplary example of anchor preschool operators stepping forward is the PAP Community Foundation (PCF) Sparkletots.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: We need more anchor preschool operators like PCF to step up, come forward and offer more of such facilities.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: While it has been a rough two years for every Singaporean, the pandemic has shown that we, as a people, are resilient and highly capable of adapting to changing circumstances.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: The era of safe distancing has encouraged innovations in our daily lifestyles, from rapid delivery of food and necessities, to e-learning and remote working.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: In the context of family life, the shift towards flexible working arrangements may have allowed some to have more time and opportunities to enjoy the company of our families and increased our ability to assist one another during trying times.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: I am glad to note that, for the past few months, our COVID-19 restrictions have been loosened to the point where many of us are able to see friends and extended family members again after a long time.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: But I also understand that the relaxed policies have also encouraged companies to recall their workers back to the office, in some cases, reverting to the pre-pandemic, five days a week schedule.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: While it is, of course, the employers' prerogative as to how they wish to run their businesses, I would like to point out that the reinstatement of mandatory office attendance will likely cause some families to cut back on quality time once again, time that they had perhaps found as a pleasant surprise amidst the bleaker days of the pandemic.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Some parents may once again become more absorbed in their work away from home as their children re-adapt to their lack of presence.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: It is also worth considering that some families with dependants have come to rely on the flexibility of being available at home to better care for them, which will cause logistical issues if they were ever recalled back to the office on a permanent basis.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: The pandemic has shown us that full remote working can be made possible across many industries and that the hybrid approach has proven to be very popular in the workforce.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Not only will families regain precious time to spend with one another, they will, in turn, become highly motivated and loyal staff members for the companies that welcome it.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: While I understand that some employees, whether due to personal preference or their particular job scope, may deem it more suitable for themselves to return physically to work, I would also like to highlight the possibility that some workers may actually prove to be more productive at home, as compared to being in the office.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: In that regard, there is really no one-size-fits-all solution.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: It is one thing to mandate that families should make the effort to create family bonding activities whenever possible, but it can be difficult to research and plan interesting outings after a long week at work.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Moreover, with rising costs due to inflation, affordability has quickly become another main concern.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: As tiny as Singapore might be in geographical terms, there are many hidden and inexpensive attractions that would make for great outing ideas for families.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Just recently, my husband and I took our three-year-old daughter to visit the Live Turtle and Tortoise Museum, which is located somewhere within Yishun and we spent a very enjoyable afternoon there.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: I believe that the community can play a bigger part in highlighting lesser-known attractions that are situated within their neighbourhoods, so that families have more options when it comes to spending precious time together.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Woodgrove has already made some progress in this regard by collaborating with community partners, such as ActiveSG, on several occasions to create grassroots events, most of which focus on physical activity and exercise.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: One example is Sporting Day, which allows families to bond through weekly sporting activities that promote play.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Friday evenings, in particular, are specially reserved for family time, when parents and their children can each pursue their own interests all within the same venue in our Marsiling-Yew Tee GRC divisions.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Another example is the school holiday camp, where families each occupies a four-man tent together and participate in camp-related activities throughout their stay.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: In addition to that, the collaborations with ActiveSG have also created special events, such as pool parties, where parents and their children can roam around the pool filled with animal floats, and terrarium creation workshops in which families learn to make their own forests in a jar.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: I hope that more funding support can be provided to partners, such as ActiveSG, to encourage even more collaborations with the community to form Made For Families interest groups and organise sports surrounding this theme on a weekly basis.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Woodgrove is prepared and looks forward to furthering our collaboration with partners, such as ActiveSG, to develop even more Made For Families events in the future in these aspects.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Besides direct collaborations with community partners, we may be able to tap on Government resources to nudge other organisations to contribute.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Many countries, such as China, have offered free admission to locals to encourage local tourism and create vibrancy at their local attractions.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: This has also supported many F&B shops at or near the attractions and created more employment opportunities.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: This will encourage families to go for outings together.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: If possible, build hawker centres to provide affordable local food at these attractions as well.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Not only will these initiatives offer families yet another opportunity to forge stronger ties with one another, but also result in a further boost for establishments within the tourism industry.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: (In English): COVID-19 has made a significant impact on individuals, families and businesses.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: It has changed our lifestyles and working habits.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Businesses must be prepared to face future disruptions, prepare their workers to stay employable and be more pro-family to retain talent in their firms.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Both employers and employees need to recognise that workplace productivity can be preserved even outside of the office through the use of technology and smart mobile devices.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: At the same time, individuals should take the initiative in strengthening familial bonds to better cope with future life challenges.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: In other words, just as businesses must have business continuity plans (BCP), so should families create their emergency preparedness plans (EPP).

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: The Government, together with the community, would always stand ready to provide the support needed for one another and create opportunities for fellow Singaporeans to embrace the various milestones in life and to care for our future generations, both in good times and in bad.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: In Woodgrove, we look forward to continuing our deep partnership with the relevant agencies and community partners to realise the plans as set forth in A Singapore Made For Families 2025 (MFF 2025) and champion Made for Families in our division.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Strong families are the bedrock of our society.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: They can be an individual's first pillar of support in good and bad times.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Strong families also help to build resilient individuals who can then be able to tackle challenges that come their way.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The Government is fully committed to strengthening our families throughout their life journey and had designated this year as the Year of Celebrating SG Families (YCF).

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Just yesterday, Deputy Prime Minister Heng Swee Keat launched A Singapore Made For Families 2025 plan (MFF 2025).

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This is a national plan that affirms our whole-of-society effort to create a family-friendly Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: It encapsulates the aspirations arising from numerous engagements with families, community partners and faith groups and builds on the work of the Alliance for Action to Strengthen Marriages and Family Relationships (AFAM).

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: I will now respond specifically to the issues Ms Hany Soh had highlighted.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: First, Ms Hany Soh spoke about the availability of infant care.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Providing access to quality, affordable preschools remains a key priority for the Government.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We have made preschools more affordable by enhancing preschool subsidies and lowering fee caps at Government-supported preschools.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: With this, we are on track to ensure that 80% of preschoolers can have a place in Government-supported preschools by about 2025.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Currently, over 90% of children are enrolled in preschool by the age of four but we recognise that the situation remains tight for the earlier years, especially in newer housing developments with many young families.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We are working closely with HDB and anchor operators to ramp up operations and manpower, where possible, to enrol more infants and children in newly opened centres in the coming months.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Similar to what Ms Hany Soh suggested, we are also exploring if it is possible to build extensions, such as through activating available void deck space or communal spaces, and also whether there is room to increase capacity and the capabilities of our existing preschools while balancing the needs of our children and our educators.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Even as we continue to develop more preschools closer to homes, we also seek parents' understanding that it is not always possible to ensure all families have a preschool right next door, near to their homes, as there can be various constraints both in terms of manpower as well as physical infrastructure constraints.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Hence, we echo Ms Hany Soh's suggestion that a possibility could be to look at preschools near workplaces.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We are already doing so – exploring this – but we would also need parents to be amenable to these suggestions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: I had earlier mentioned working closely with anchor operators to ramp up operations and manpower.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: These include increasing recruitment, reallocating and optimising manpower.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We hope that the recently announced salary revisions of a 10% to 30% pay raise for preschool educators can help to meet this demand but, fundamentally, to echo what Deputy Prime Minister Lawrence Wong had said before, we, as a society, have to value the work of social service professionals and early childhood educators in order to attract more people into the sector.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Without a core workforce to support our early childhood sector, we will face constraints growing capacity.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: I agree with Ms Hany Soh that working from home has given many parents the joy of spending more time with their families and that working parents sometimes need the flexibility to leave office earlier or to adjust their work schedules to tend to family commitments.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This brings me to the second point on flexible work arrangements (FWAs) and the critical role that employers play here.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The pandemic has made FWAs like telecommuting and staggered work hours much more prevalent, such as the hybrid work arrangements practised by the Public Service.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: More employers have also come to realise how FWAs can help them both strengthen business resilience and enhance their ability to attract and retain talent.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Employees also appreciate how FWAs enable them to spend more quality family time, which, in turn, energises them to go the extra mile in their work.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: When implemented well, FWAs achieve a win-win outcome for employers and employees.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This is why the Government and our tripartite partners have urged employers to sustain their FWAs through the Tripartite Statement released in April this year.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The tripartite partners have been steadily bringing more companies on board the Tripartite Standard on FWAs and we encourage employers who intend to or already provide FWAs to adopt the Standard and be recognised as a progressive employer of choice.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: By 2024, we will introduce the Tripartite Guidelines on FWAs, which will require all employers to consider requests for FWAs fairly and properly.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Of course, family time is not just about quantity but also quality.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The AFAM's Focal Area 3: Parenting Together has been working together with our community partners and myself to share parenting tips to better support quality family time.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: I note Ms Soh's suggestion on the importance of having affordable options for family bonding activities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Although the SingapoRediscovers Vouchers scheme has ended, there are still deals and promotions for family activities, such as those by our Made For Families partners.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: As Ms Soh has mentioned, there are many hidden gems in Singapore that families can discover together.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: From child-friendly museums to nature playgrounds, the options for the perfect family day out are endless.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Quite a few of these activities are admission-free and of high quality, such as the heritage trails found around the various heartlands in Singapore that allow families to discover the untold stories behind our well-known neighbourhoods.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: At the grassroots level, families can find workshops, carnivals and festival celebrations within their neighbourhoods.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: I am glad to hear of the initiatives Ms Hany Soh mentioned.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: With the school holidays coming up, families can look forward to activities and courses run by People's Association (PA) under their School Holidays Series, which are specially curated courses catered for families.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Parents can also spend quality time bonding with their children through parent-child craft workshops or learn more through various parenting courses.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The Government is committed to doing its part and we will work closely with employers, community partners and the wider society so that all can play this very important role to nurture a supportive ecosystem for families to live, play and work in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: In this Year of Celebrating SG Families, it is timely for us to reflect on how each and every one of us can come together in our own ways to make Singapore truly a home, a playground and a caring society that values and supports families at every stage of life.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Let us, collectively, work towards achieving A Singapore Made for Families.
